messages.text: South African aviation regulator probes low jet flypast

metadata.summary: A low flypast by two passenger jets before South Africa's second Test against New Zealand in Cape Town, which drew safety concerns, is being reviewed.
metadata.content: South Africa vs New Zealand: Cape Town stadium low jet flypast probed by South African aviation authority | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to content South Africa vs New Zealand: Cape Town stadium low jet flypast probed by South African aviation authority South Africa's aviation authority is reviewing a low flypast by two passenger jets, with plans for another flyover withdrawn; watch every minute of New Zealand's tour of South Africa exclusively live on Sky Sports Wednesday 2 September 2026 17:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment two planes were involved in a very close call during a low flyover before South Africa and New Zealand's rugby union Test in Cape Town A low flypast by two passenger jets before South Africa's second Test against New Zealand in Cape Town, which drew safety concerns, is being reviewed. The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) said it had obtained flight data recordings and requested additional information from Airlink as part of its assessment into the incident involving two passenger jets which passed within 100 metres of the DHL Stadium roof on Saturday. A full report with recommendations will be issued once the review is complete. "It is therefore critical that we interrogate this past weekend's events … to determine if there were any safety concerns which warrant a review," the agency said in a statement.
